The concept of a QCD effective charge, which defines an evolution scheme for collinear parton distribution and fragmentation functions that is all-orders exact, is then used to deliver predictions for the $x$-dependence of these DFs at the scale $\zeta_{2} = 2\,$GeV. Although the approach is largely algebraic, its predictions remain viable after comparisons with results obtained using computationally intensive methods. Thus, given the scarcity of data that can today be used for inference of proton transversity DFs, it may be worth using the results herein to inform and constrain related experiments and phenomenological fits.

title: Cold Magnetized Quark Matter under Compact-Star Conditions
summary: We investigate the phase structure of cold magnetized two-flavor quark matter under compact-star conditions within a nonlocal chiral quark model with separable interactions. Electric charge neutrality and beta equilibrium are imposed in order to describe matter under realistic neutron-star conditions, while nonlocality is implemented through a Gaussian form factor. We find that low and moderate magnetic fields reduce the critical chemical potential for chiral symmetry restoration, signaling inverse magnetic catalysis. For stronger magnetic fields, the critical chemical potential becomes nearly independent of the magnetic field strength, Compared with the isospin-symmetric case, the combined effects of charge neutrality and beta equilibrium shift the first-order chiral transition to slightly higher chemical potentials, indicating that compact-star constraints delay the onset of chiral symmetry restoration. We further show that charge neutrality and beta equilibrium modify the de Haas--van Alphen oscillations in the quark density, shifting the Landau-level thresholds for the $u$ and $d$ quarks in opposite directions relative to the isospin-symmetric case. The effect on the chiral transition is small ($\sim 5$MeV) for fields $B\lesssim 10^{19}$G, relevant for magnetar interiors, and becomes sizable only for $B\gtrsim 3\times10^{19}$G. These results highlight the importance of incorporating realistic stellar conditions in studies of the QCD phase diagram at high baryon density.

title: Unpolarized Generalized Parton Distributions of the Nucleon in a Covariant Quark-Diquark Approach
summary: We study the unpolarized generalized parton distributions (GPDs) of the nucleon in a covariant quark-diquark approach, in which both scalar and axial-vector diquarks are treated as composite subsystems. Motivated by previous form factor studies, we introduce a vertex correction based on the pion cloud picture as a first exploratory treatment of pion cloud effects at the GPD level, in order to improve the description of $E^q(\xi, x, t)$ and related magnetic observables. At the model input scale, only valence quarks are included. With the vertex correction, the electromagnetic form factors $G_{E, M}$ and the mass form factor $A$ obtained from the Mellin moments of the GPDs agree well with those obtained from direct calculations. The vertex correction brings the evolved charge weighted distribution $\sum{e^q E^q(\xi, x, t)}$ closer to the phenomenological parametrization. The correction shifts transverse strength from the central region toward the peripheral region, consistent with the long range character of the pion cloud contribution. The transverse structure results further suggest a harder longitudinal momentum distribution in the central region of the nucleon than in its periphery. Furthermore, the evolved real part of the proton Compton form factor, $\mathrm{Re} \mathcal{H}(\xi, t)$, has a reasonable magnitude and follows the main trend of the Quantum Deep Neural Networks (QDNN) extraction. In addition, $\mathrm{Re} \mathcal{H}$ may be more sensitive to the ERBL region than the other physical quantities calculated in this work.

title: Coupled-channel pole structure and bare-state mixing of bottom-strange heavy-quark spin partners
summary: Motivated by the observation of the $B_{s0}^*(5700)$ and the heavy-quark symmetry relations connecting the $DK$, $D^*K$, $\bar{B}K$, and $\bar B^*K$ systems, we investigate whether the same chiral dynamics can generate negative-parity partners dominated by the $\bar B_1K$ and $\bar B_2^*K$ components. We further examine how nearby bare bottom-strange states reshape the pole spectrum through coupled-channel mixing. Both the relevant $S$-wave scattering and the lower-lying $P$-wave decay channels are explicitly included in the coupled-channel calculation. In the absence of bare states, the interaction generates two negative-parity poles near $6.15$ GeV. Coupling the hadronic channels to the corresponding quark-model configurations leads to a richer two-pole structure in each sector, with the pole masses, widths, and channel residues governed by the interplay between the bare states and the hadronic dynamics. In particular, the inclusion of the bare states substantially increases the widths of the negative-parity poles with the larger $S$-wave molecular components. The resulting correlated patterns in the pole spectrum provide testable signatures for future studies of excited bottom-strange mesons.

title: Long-lived linear slow roll near critical and spinodal points in soft-wall AdS/QCD
summary: We systematically investigate the real-time evolution of the chiral condensate near critical and spinodal points within soft-wall AdS/QCD, focusing primarily on the long-lived prethermalization stage, in contrast to the conventional early transients and late-time relaxation. While the quasi-steady nature of this stage has been previously identified, we demonstrate that it is intrinsically a continuous linear slow roll, fundamentally distinct from the asymptotic critical slowing down at late times. By showing that the bulk evolution adiabatically follows the boundary condensate on a slow configuration space, we analytically project the 5D partial differential equation onto a boundary first-order Ginzburg-Landau (GL) equation. We find that the long lifetime of this linear regime is protected by a ``double-zero'' condition: the simultaneous vanishing of the local potential gradient (suppressing the drift velocity) and curvature (suppressing the acceleration). This geometric flatness inherently emerges at the second-order point and both first-order spinodal endpoints. Crucially, this behavior is not a fine-tuned artifact, but a generic consequence of the effective potential landscape intrinsic to these phase-transition endpoints, persisting across a broad class of physically relevant initial conditions and temperature quenches. A local short-time expansion further relates the interval duration to the potential curvature and its higher-order derivatives, in good agreement with our numerical simulations. This work establishes a direct link between the local structure of phase-transition endpoints and the dynamical evolution of the long-lived intermediate stage of the condensate.

title: Gravitational Form Factors and Transverse Mechanical Structure of the Charged Kaon in a Two-Fock-Sector Light-Front Hamiltonian
summary: We study the electromagnetic and gravitational form factors of the charged kaon in a light-front Hamiltonian model with coupled $|u\bar s\rangle$ and $|u\bar s g\rangle$ Fock sectors. We solve the coupled Hamiltonian in a longitudinal Jacobi and transverse harmonic-oscillator basis, with the interaction strength fixed by the kaon mass. The momentum form factors are extracted from $T^{++}$, while the stress form factors are obtained from the transverse shear projection of the QCD Belinfante energy-momentum tensor, including diagonal, sector-changing, and constrained-field contributions. The strange antiquark carries the largest fraction of the kaon's longitudinal momentum, whereas the gluon carries only $2.05\%$. Despite this small momentum fraction, the gluon contributes $42.4\%$ of $|D_K(0)|$, for which we obtain $D_K(0)=-2.03610$. The charge and transverse momentum radii are $0.5178\pm0.0278\,\mathrm{fm}$ and $0.3394\pm0.0113\,\mathrm{fm}$, respectively, with uncertainties estimated from mass and basis variations. We obtain the transverse mechanical distributions using two ultraviolet continuations of the directly calculated $D$ form factors beyond $Q^2=2\,\mathrm{GeV}^2$. Both continuations give positive pressure at small transverse distances and negative pressure at larger distances. The corresponding transverse mechanical radii are $0.4616\pm0.0130\,\mathrm{fm}$ and $0.4768\pm0.0132\,\mathrm{fm}$, both larger than the transverse momentum radius. The central pressure changes substantially between the two continuations, whereas the pressure zero and mechanical radii vary much less.

title: Geoneutrinos (and reactor neutrinos) do not visibly decay
summary:
Neutrinos that decay on their way to a detector arrive depleted, more so at low energies, where time dilation lengthens their lifetime the least. Geoneutrinos---electron antineutrinos from the radioactive decay of uranium and thorium inside the Earth---have energies of a few MeV and travel up to the diameter of the Earth. We use them to test neutrino decay for the first time. We compute the geoneutrino signal at Borexino, KamLAND, SNO+, and JUNO for visible decay, in which the daughter neutrinos are themselves detected, and compare it against their published data. We find no evidence of decay that holds across Earth models. Combining the four experiments, we limit the decay $
u_1 	o 
u_3$ in the inverted mass ordering at 90% C.L.: $	au_1/m_1 > 3.7 	imes 10^{-9}$ s eV$^{-1}$ when the radiogenic power of the Earth is left free and $	au_1/m_1 > 4.4 	imes 10^{-9}$ to $1.6 	imes 10^{-8}$ s eV$^{-1}$ when it is taken from Earth models. With an Earth model assumed, the geoneutrinos set the limit; with the power free, the antineutrinos from nuclear reactors that the same experiments detect count as much as the geoneutrinos. These are the first terrestrial limits on the visible decay of $
u_1$.

title: Role of excited hyperons in $K^{*}Ξ$ production via $K^{-}N$ scattering
summary: We investigate the production mechanism of $K^-N\to K^*\Xi$ and the role of high-mass excited hyperons within an effective Lagrangian approach, using a combined fit to cross section and polarization data for $K^-p\to K^{*+}\Xi^-$. The model includes $s$- and $u$-channel exchanges of the ground-state $\Lambda$ and $\Sigma$ hyperons, together with $s$-channel contributions from $\Lambda(2325)$ and $\Sigma(2230)$. The pronounced near-threshold enhancement of the total cross section is driven mainly by these excited hyperons, whereas $u$-channel exchange dominates at backward angles at higher energies. Polarization results show that both the $K^*$ spin-density matrix elements and the $\Xi$ recoil polarization are sensitive to excited-hyperon contributions near threshold. Notably, the latter remains sensitive to interference involving excited-hyperon amplitudes even at higher energies. Moreover, with the same fitted parameters and no additional free parameters, the predicted cross sections for $K^-p\to K^{*0}\Xi^0$ and $K^-n\to K^{*0}\Xi^-$ agree well with available measurements. Finally, a Dalitz analysis of $K^-p \to K^{*+}\Xi^- \to K\pi\Xi^-$, together with existing $K\pi\Xi^-$ cross section data, indicates the feasibility of reconstructing $K^{*+}\Xi^-$ through this final state. These results suggest that $K^*\Xi$ production provides a valuable reaction channel for investigating high-mass excited hyperons and their hadronic couplings, and offers theoretical guidance for future experimental measurements.

title: Probing dimension-six SMEFT operators in heavy-quark sector at future muon collider
summary: We investigate the sensitivity to the dimension-six Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT) operators which define the interactions of heavy-quarks with electroweak gauge bosons and with leptons via the process $\mu^- \mu^+ \rightarrow Wtb$, followed by leptonic W-boson decays, at a 10 TeV muon collider with an integrated luminosity of 10 ab$^{-1}$. Signal and background events are generated at leading order using MadGraph5aMC@NLO, interfaced with Pythia 8 for parton showering and hadronization, and passed through Delphes 3.5 for fast detector simulation. The 95% confidence level (C.L.) limits on nine Wilson coefficients are derived using a cut-based method for two $b$-tagging working points (70% and 90% efficiencies). These limits are significantly tighter than those currently reported by the CMS Collaboration; furthermore, these results highlight the advanced potential of a future high-energy muon collider to investigate new physics within the electroweak sector through precise measurements of heavy-quark interactions.

title: Improving Sensitivity to Rare Processes at the LHC with Geodesic-Aware Graph Neural Networks
comment: 42 pages including references; 12 figures and 8 tables
summary: Rare processes at the Large Hadron Collider often lead to final states with quarks, for which the dominant backgrounds contain the same reconstructed objects as the signal. The colour structure of the hard process, imprinted on the pattern of soft QCD radiation, carries information that is largely left unused by standard analyses. We introduce a geometric representation of this colour flow by mapping hadronic constituents onto the unit sphere through a modified inverse stereographic projection centred on a pair of jets selected as a colour-singlet resonance candidate. The jet separation defines a circular region whose interior and exterior are mapped to opposite hemispheres, allowing a graph neural network to exploit the resulting radiation pattern using geodesic distances. As a benchmark, we consider flavour-changing neutral interactions of the top quark with the Higgs boson at $\sqrt{s}=13.6$~TeV, through associated $tH$ production and $t\bar t$ production with one top quark undergoing a $t\to qH$ decay, where $q=u,c$, focusing on subsequent $H\to b\bar b$ and leptonically top quark decays in both channels. Relative to a baseline graph neural network operating in the $(\eta,\phi)$ plane, the geodesic-aware network improves the expected 95\% confidence-level limits on $\mathrm{BR}(t\to uH)$ and $\mathrm{BR}(t\to cH)$ by about an order of magnitude, to $1.1\times10^{-4}$ and $8.3\times10^{-5}$ for an assumed integrated luminosity of $139~\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$. The approach can also be applied to searches for other colour-singlet resonances decaying into quarks or gluons.

title: Search for Heavy Charged Higgs Bosons in Boosted Top and Bottom Quark Final States at a 1.4 TeV Future Lepton Collider
summary: The discovery potential for heavy charged Higgs bosons $H^\pm$ decaying into a top-bottom quark pair is investigated at a future $e^+e^-$ collider operating at $\sqrt{s}=1.4~\mathrm{TeV}$. The study considers charged Higgs masses between 200 and 600 GeV within all four Yukawa types of the two-Higgs-doublet model (2HDM). The boosted $tb$ final state is explored using complementary cut-based and machine-learning analyses based on boosted decision trees (BDT). The expected signal significance and sensitivity contours in the $(m_{H^\pm},\tan\beta)$ plane are obtained for each Yukawa type. The resulting sensitivity extends to regions of the 2HDM parameter space beyond the projected reach of the High-Luminosity LHC (HL-LHC), demonstrating the complementary potential of a future high-energy lepton collider to probe heavy charged Higgs bosons.

title: Doubly heavy open--flavor tetraquarks within the relativistic quark model
summary: Mass spectra of the ground, orbitally and radially excited states of doubly heavy open--flavor tetraquarks are calculated within the relativistic quark model based on the quasipotential approach and quantum chromodynamics. Tetraquarks are considered as bound states of a heavy diquark $\mathrm{QQ^{\prime}}$ ($\mathrm{Q,Q^{\prime} = c,b}$) and a light antidiquark $\mathrm{\overline{qq^{\prime}}}$ ($\mathrm{q,q^{\prime} = u,d,s}$). The diquark--antidiquark interaction quasipotential includes both spin--independent and spin--dependent relativistic contributions. The finite sizes of the diquark and antidiquark are taken into account via the form factors of their interaction with gluons. Masses of the ground ($1S$) and excited ($1P$, $2S$, $1D$, $2P$, $3S$) states are calculated including the mixing of states with the same observable quantum numbers $J^{P}$ but different spins $S$. The obtained masses are compared with the lowest allowed thresholds for strong fall--apart decays into a pair of heavy--light mesons in $S$--wave. Most of the states lie significantly above these thresholds. However, several states, predominantly orbital excitations with large $J$, lie below or slightly above the corresponding thresholds and, thus, could be promising candidates for experimental observation. The number of such near--threshold states increases for tetraquarks containing bottom quarks. The predicted mass of the ground state of the $\mathrm{cc\overline{ud}}$ tetraquark with $J^{P}=1^{+}$ is consistent with the experimentally observed $\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{cc}}(3875)^{+}$ state.

title: Hadronic production of excited $B_c$ mesons at the LHC
summary: We study the hadronic production of ground-state and excited $B_c$ mesons at the LHC for $\sqrt{S}=13$ TeV within the framework of NRQCD factorization at leading order in QCD. The calculation includes the $1S$, $1P$, and $2S$ multiplets, with both color-singlet and color-octet contributions to direct $1P$ production. For $p_T>0.2$ GeV, the summed production cross section is $336.04^{+275.80}_{-175.43}$ nb; the quoted uncertainty combines the specified heavy-quark mass and common-scale variations and does not include PDF-set differences. The NNPDF3.0 and MSHT20LO predictions are approximately $23\%$--$24\%$ below the CT18LO result. With the adopted radiative-transition branching fractions, $2S$ feed-down increases the total $1P$ yield from $34.73$ to $75.34$ nb. The relative enhancement differs markedly among the four spectroscopic states, ranging from $38\%$ for $1^1P_1$ to $262\%$ for $1^3P_0$, and it reorders their integrated production hierarchy. Within the set of states included here, the ratio of the $1P$ yield to the inclusive ground-state yield increases from $0.103$ to $0.224$. We present the state-resolved distributions and the dependence of direct production on kinematic cuts, parton distributions, quark masses, and scale choices. These results illustrate the potential impact of $2S$ feed-down on the relative yields of the lowest $P$-wave $B_c$ states.

title: No room for $X(2370)$ exceptionalism: the glueball interpretation warrants caution
summary: Motivated by recent BESIII claims that $X(2370)$ is a pseudoscalar glueball candidate, we reanalyze several radiative $J/\psi$ decays into three pseudoscalars, $J/\psi\to\gamma PPP$, with emphasis on the $X(2370)$ region. A simultaneous analysis of the three invariant-mass projections in $J/\psi\to\gamma K_S^0K_S^0\eta^\prime$, including the pseudoscalar states $X(1835)$, $X(2120)$, $\eta(2225)$, $X(2370)$, $X(2500)$, and $\eta_c$, reproduces the observed dip near $2.2~\mathrm{GeV}$ and the enhancement near $2.4~\mathrm{GeV}$ through coherent interference, without invoking the additional broad $X(2800)$ component employed in the BESIII partial-wave analysis. We further analyze $J/\psi\to\gamma\pi^0\pi^0\eta$ and $J/\psi\to\gamma K_S^0K_S^0\pi^0$ by including both pseudoscalar and axial-vector contributions, and show that multiple excited meson states collectively describe the data. The absence of a prominent $X(2370)$ signal in the $K^*(892)$ region can be understood from differing orbital angular-momentum requirements rather than flavor-singlet suppression alone. Our results indicate that $X(2370)$ is not exceptional compared with the other reported pseudoscalar states in this mass region. Therefore, interpreting $X(2370)$ as a glueball-dominated state should be treated with caution.

title: Total Angular Momentum Assignments in the Hadron Spectrum
summary: Predicting the total angular momentum $J$ for hadronic resonances whose spins have not yet been experimentally determined constitutes an important step in the spectroscopy of observed hadrons. In the present study, we develop a data-driven model in order to predict the value of $ J $ for hadrons with unknown spins using a dataset of known mesons and baryons from the PDG, including information on their quark content, isospin, parity, mass and other spectroscopic features. In particular, we employ XGBoost classifiers along with nested optimization in order to discover spectroscopic patterns across different hadronic sectors. We also prepare a systematic list of hadrons with unknown or poorly determined values of $ J $, and study spin-parity assignments for those hadrons. Since the parity hypothesis is taken as an input to the model, our model predicts the value of $ J $ conditional on a given parity hypothesis rather than independently determining the full $J^P$ assignment. Our predictions for several theoretically studied states show good agreement with results from quark models, QCD sum rules, molecular models, and other phenomenological approaches, while predictions for some other states differ from existing theoretical assignments. These differences motivate further theoretical investigations and may be tested by future experimental measurements.

title: Active Learning and Genetic Search for Discrete Abelian Flavor Model Building
summary: The sequential breaking of discrete flavor symmetries provides a theoretical framework that can explain quark mass and mixing angle hierarchies. Each model is identified by its field content, charge assignments and symmetry breaking pattern, leading to an enormous space of possible models; this motivates the investigation of computational approaches for identifying promising candidates. In this work, we focus on quark flavor models with the flavor symmetry group $G_F=(\mathbb{Z}_2)^p$, where $p$ is a positive integer; operators involving flavon fields which spontaneously break the flavor symmetry determine the size of the Yukawa matrix entries. We consider two search strategies: an active learning search employing a random forest regressor and a genetic search. The generation of candidate models is automated and models are evaluated using a loss function that takes into account the logarithmic discrepancy between the model prediction and target observable values as well as penalties for model complexity. We find that both our active learning and genetic algorithms significantly outperform random model generation, which we use as a control; our active learning approach identifies lower-loss models faster (i.e., with fewer exact model evaluations) than our genetic search, though each ultimately finds successful models. Our results support the effectiveness of active learning and evolutionary optimization as approaches to automate the search for promising models based on discrete flavor symmetries.

title: A New GUT
comment: 5 pages, 2 figures. Supplementary material contains 11 pages, 1 figure
summary: We present a new class of 4-dimensional Grand Unified Theories where the gauge sectors of the standard model have a novel embedding in the unified group that does not factor through an $SU(5)$ subgroup. The smallest example has gauge algebra $\frak{su}(12)$ and an anomaly-free spectrum that produces the three standard model generations with no additional chiral matter. The embedding predicts the axion-photon anomaly ratio $E/N=2/3$ and the weak mixing angle $\sin^2\theta_W=1/2$ at the unification scale. Gauge-mediated proton decay proceeds through flipped-$SU(5)$-like operators and the minimally charged smooth monopole carries two Dirac charge units. The global gauge group can be $SU(12)$ or $SU(12)/\mathbb{Z}_2$, with the former allowing color singlets of half-integer electric charge. We develop a GUT bootstrap to constrain $SU(n)$ embeddings with three generations and no additional chiral matter. For unified fermions in up to two-index representations, we prove that all new embeddings arise from the $SU(8m+4)$ family, including flavor unified models for $m \geq 2$.

title: On the cosmic window for neutrino self-interactions
summary:
Neutrino self-interactions ($
u$SI) beyond the Standard Model have arisen as a promising probe of new physics in cosmology. In this Letter, we show that $
u$SI emerging in the low-energy limit of renormalizable theories implies resonant mediator behavior. We identify two regions for $
u$SI: (i) neutrinos become tightly coupled with background evolution; for the first time, we establish how this evolution modifies the Boltzmann hierarchy equations (BHEs), and (ii) resonant $
u$SI dominates the dynamics with negligible background evolution, relevant for mediator masses $\sim 10^{-6}-1$ MeV. In region (i), before matter-radiation equality, neutrino free-streaming is determined by the effective four-fermion interaction, known as the heavy-mediator limit (HML); we explore the impact of background evolution on this scenario, and from our modified BHEs, we show that self-interacting dark radiation scenarios require larger couplings than previously estimated to mimic $
u$SI. Region (ii) shows that the simplest realization of $
u$SI mediated by a (pseudo)scalar particle leads to an extra radiation contribution of $\Delta N_{m eff}^{m CMB} \approx 0$, instead of the commonly quoted $\simeq 0.12$, at the CMB epoch. Overall, we highlight that our findings should be considered in any plausible scenario involving $
u$SI.

title: Pole parameters of the $f_2(1270)$ and $f_2'(1525)$ from a coupled-channel analysis of the radiative $J/ψ$ multipoles
summary: We determine the pole parameters of $f_2(1270)$ and $f_2'(1525)$ from the combined fit to the isoscalar $D$-wave $\pi\pi$ phase shift, the $\pi\pi\to K\bar K$ modulus, and the BESIII $J/\psi\to\gamma\pi^0\pi^0$ and $\gamma K_SK_S$ data: all three $2^{++}$ multipoles $E1$, $M2$ and $E3$, and the $M2$-$E1$ phases. The hadronic amplitude is a two-channel $K$-matrix with two poles and all parameters free, so that no resonance information is taken from the Particle Data Group. The radiative decay amplitudes are written as a coupled-channel Muskhelishvili-Omnès representation, with the Omnès matrix generated by that hadronic amplitude. The left-hand cuts, which carry the production dynamics, are approximated by a linear subtraction polynomial in the physical region. The model-independent kinematic constraints among the $J=2$ helicity amplitudes are implemented explicitly. The fit describes all $358$ points with $\chi^2/N=1.29$ and gives $\sqrt{s_p}=(1267.5\pm1.3\pm2.6)-i\,\frac{1}{2}\,(175.5\pm2.4\pm7.4)\ \mathrm{MeV}$ for the $f_2(1270)$ and $(1514.8\pm2.8\pm1.5)-i\,\frac{1}{2}\,(80.4\pm3.4\pm4.8)\ \mathrm{MeV}$ for the $f_2'(1525)$, where the first uncertainty is statistical, from a parametric bootstrap with the data errors rescaled by $\sqrt{\chi^2/N}$ of each set, and the second systematic, from $17$ variations of the analysis.

title: Locally infrared finite two-loop amplitudes for multi Higgs production in association with one jet
summary: We study the two-loop amplitudes for multi-Higgs production through a massive top-quark loop in association with one jet. We consider the quark-antiquark channel with a final-state gluon, $q\bar q\to g+nH$ although our construction applies to crossed channel as well. We utilize (non-local in momentum space) Ward identities to factorize longitudinal and gauge degrees of freedom through exact identities between Feynman graphs without reference to an infrared region. In the genuine two loop topologies, we replace the internal gluons by their physical degrees of freedom and show that the resulting amplitude is free of collinear singularities. The only remaining infrared divergence is a soft singularity that can be identified with a change of reference gauge vector. We construct explicit soft counterterms for these singularities, obtaining a locally infrared-finite representation. We verify that the factorized longitudinal degrees of freedom reproduce the remaining infrared poles of the original Feynman graphs. Our formalism requires no counter-terms for collinear finiteness or for manifesting Ward identities in various regions since we perform a decomposition of covariant gauge Feynman graphs. We expect its extension to more complicated processes to eliminate all collinear singularities--particularly in the initial state.

title: Comment on "Exact, nonsingular black holes from a phantom DBI field as primordial dark matter"
comment: 2 pages. Includes supplemental material. Comment on arXiv:2511.14047
summary: We demonstrate that the metric and scalar configuration proposed in Ref.~[1] do not satisfy the complete set of field equations of the Dirac-Born-Infeld (DBI) field theory minimally coupled to general relativity on a radial domain containing the event horizon. The physical DBI branch for this gravitational setup terminates outside the event horizon. Thus, the proposed configuration does not describe a black hole solution of that theory.

title: Projected Sensitivity of a Differential Torsion Sensor for Tests of the Weak Equivalence Principle
summary: Tests of the weak equivalence principle (WEP) are among the most sensitive probes of new long-range, composition-dependent interactions beyond general relativity and the Standard Model. We evaluate the potential of a differential torsion sensor, which combines long mechanical coherence times with optical-cavity readout and common-mode rejection, for laboratory WEP tests and fifth-force searches. For a representative configuration based on an existing prototype, with Be-Ti test masses and 180 days of coherent integration, the projected noise-limited sensitivity to the Eötvös parameter is $\eta\simeq7.5\times10^{-16}$ and $2.4\times10^{-16}$ for signal modulation at 2 and 20 mHz, respectively, below current ground-based torsion-balance limits. For a baryon-coupled Yukawa interaction sourced by the Earth, the corresponding projected sensitivity to the coupling strength is $\alpha\simeq3.1\times10^{-13}$ and $9.8\times10^{-14}$ for ranges $\lambda\gtrsim10^{7}$ m. We identify the modulation scheme, the material contrast, and the source geometry as the main factors that set the projected reach, and the control of systematic couplings as the main experimental requirement for attaining it. These results indicate that differential torsion sensors are a promising platform for future laboratory WEP tests.

title: Precision Measurements of the Effective Leptonic Weak Mixing Angle at Hadron Colliders
comment: 19 pages, 7 figures, 1 table. Review article submitted to Physics Reports
summary: We review precision determinations of the effective leptonic weak mixing angle, $\sin^2\theta^\ell_{\mathrm{eff}}$, from Drell-Yan angular asymmetries at the Tevatron and the LHC. As statistical uncertainties have dramatically decreased, parton distribution function (PDF) uncertainty now dominates the most precise hadron-collider results. We describe the angular observables, electroweak calculation schemes, and advanced methods such as replica reweighting and Hessian profiling, used to constrain PDFs directly from measured angular distributions. To identify the origin of differences between modern PDF sets (e.g., CT18, MSHT20, NNPDF) in the extracted mixing angle, we employ a simplified leading-order Z-pole calculation that separates quark-flavor production weights from quark-direction dilution. We demonstrate how these PDF-induced differences can be mitigated by incorporating complementary constraints from W/Z cross-section ratios and W-boson decay asymmetries. Furthermore, we discuss the requirements for a common reinterpretation and future combination of LHC measurements, highlighting how correlated PDF uncertainties limit the ultimate combined precision. Finally, we outline future prospects, including complementary measurements in $Z+b$ production and high-mass tests of the running $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ weak mixing angle.

title: LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA stochastic constraints on first-order phase transitions: A tale of priors
summary: We re-examine the methodology for constraining cosmological first-order phase transitions from gravitational-wave searches using Bayesian statistical analysis. Specifically, we use results from LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA searches for a stochastic gravitational wave background during observing runs O1--O4a. We explore multiple prior choices across three categories of fit parameters: geometrical parameters, thermodynamical parameters of phase transitions, and the parameters of an Abelian Higgs particle physics model. Our key finding is that the constraints on most parameters describing gravitational waves from a phase transition depend strongly on the prior. Consequently, the data do not yet allow to derive robust constraints on these parameters. Besides, even if a parameter is meaningfully constrained, the upper limit can vary significantly with the prior range. We provide practical recommendations for assessing the robustness of parameter estimates and guidelines for rigorously testing prior independence in future analyses.

title: Light fermions can trigger a Brout-Englert-Higgs effect
summary: The Brout-Englert-Higgs effect produces the masses of the Standard Model particles. However, the cause of this effect is unknown. Beyond-the-Standard-Model theories aim to find the source of this effect, for example using a composite Higgs and dynamically generating its vacuum expectation value. In this paper, we show evidence from lattice simulations with vectorially coupled fermions and without Yukawa couplings that the Brout-Englert-Higgs effect could be triggered by the light masses of fermions. This suggests that an explanation entirely within the Standard Model could be possible. Moreover, our results are consistent with weak couplings and fermions can only impact the Higgs potential at NNLO. This implies a so far unidentified mechanism in an SU(2) scalar-fermion-gauge system that produces a non-zero vacuum expectation value. In addition, we find that the transition from a QCD-like behavior to a Higgs-like behavior happens when the fermion mass falls below twice the W/Z mass: a threshold that is integer valued but not connected to other critical physical behavior.
